summary: Lower a stable `super.method(...)` call to C# `base.method(...)` only when the base prototype property is a known unmodified method.

target.notes: Emit `base.$m(...)`; this preserves the current receiver while selecting the known base implementation under closed-world prototype conditions.

semantics.lookup_start: base prototype of method home object

caveats: JavaScript super lookup is property lookup, not a statically bound base call, unless the prototype is proven stable.
references: ECMAScript Super Calls and Super Property: https://tc39.es/ecma262/#sec-super-keyword

tests.name: base method call
tests.input: class B { m(){return 1;} } class D extends B { m(){return super.m()+1;} } console.log(new D().m());

tests.name: edge: later base prototype patch excluded
tests.input: class B { m(){return 1;} } class D extends B { m(){return super.m();} } B.prototype.m=()=>3; console.log(new D().m());
tests.expected_behavior: prints 3; C# base.m() would still target compiled code, so this rule must not match
